patch.objective: File analysis (Strings, VirusTotal, Yet another recursive acronym (YARA)) and sandboxing (Joe Sandbox, Cuckoo Sandbox)

sources.cite: CompTIA CySA+ CS0-004 Exam Objectives, Version 2.0 (exam launched 2026-06-23): tools and techniques for analysis, including file analysis (strings, YARA) and sandboxing
sources.note: The objectives were read for the course and REQ-238 on 2026-11-11; not re-read for this band. The objective title is the course's own wording.

sources.cite: NIST SP 800-83 Rev. 1, Guide to Malware Incident Prevention and Handling for Desktops and Laptops (July 2013)
sources.note: Relevant text: 4.2.4 active analysis 'best performed on malware test systems instead of production hosts'; 4.2.2.2 'Writing a custom IPS or IDS signature that identifies infected hosts is often a highly effective technique'; 4.3.4 disconnect infected hosts and 'consider blocking all access to the external host'; 4.4 'For many malware incidents, simple disinfection is not feasible, so it is necessary to rebuild all infected hosts'. Read 2026-11-16 in the PDF through two summarizing fetches.

sources.cite: YARA documentation 4.4.0, Writing YARA rules: a rule has an identifier, an optional meta section, strings and a required condition; text strings in quotes (nocase, wide modifiers), hex strings in braces; conditions such as 'all of them', '2 of ($a*)' and filesize
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch. The rules in the case are shown as text and never run.

sources.cite: SigmaHQ, Sigma rule conventions (sigma-specification, sigmahq_conventions.md): required fields include title, id, status, description, references, author, date, tags, logsource, falsepositives and level; detection holds search identifiers and a condition; 'All newly created rules must start with a status of experimental'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch; undated page.

sources.cite: MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001, Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder (version 2.1, last modified 2026-11-04): the per-user and machine Run and RunOnce keys and the Startup folders; adversaries may masquerade Registry entries as legitimate programs
IETF RFC 5737 (IPv4 documentation blocks 192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) and RFC 2606 (reserved names example.com, example.net, example.org, .test, .example, .invalid)
sources.note: Every address and domain in the case is from these ranges; checked by the sandbox lint. Read for REQ-231 on 2026-11-11; not re-read.
The sample, its behavior, the second host and the attacker's timing are fictional and simplified for teaching; nothing in the case is a real sample, a real indicator or runnable.
